definition: Neural Network Exchange Format (NNEF) is an artificial neural network data exchange format developed by the Khronos Group.
details: It is intended to reduce machine learning deployment fragmentation by enabling a rich mix of neural network training tools and inference engines to be used by applications across a diverse range of devices and platforms.

explainer.lead: Neural Network Exchange Format (NNEF) is an artificial neural network data exchange format developed by the Khronos Group. It aims to reduce machine learning deployment fragmentation by enabling interoperability between training tools and inference engines.

tiers.eli5: It's a common language that lets different AI programs share their models easily, like a universal file format for documents.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use NNEF to transfer trained models between frameworks and deploy them on diverse devices. A pitfall is that not all frameworks support NNEF natively, requiring conversion steps.
tiers.paperLevel: Neural Network Exchange Format (NNEF) is an artificial neural network data exchange format developed by the Khronos Group. It is intended to reduce machine learning deployment fragmentation by enabling a rich mix of training tools and inference engines across devices and platforms.

explainer.example: A model trained in TensorFlow can be exported to NNEF and then imported into an inference engine on a mobile device.
